An interactive editor for viewing, entering and editing data

Source: R/data_edit.R
data_edit.Rd

data_edit is a shiny application built on the MIT-licensed 'Tabulator' JavaScript library that is designed to make it easy to interactively view, enter or edit data without any coding. data_edit is also a wrapper for any reading or writing function to make it easy to interactively update data saved to file, and can edit tables stored in a database.

Usage

data_edit(
  x = NULL,
  col_bind = NULL,
  col_edit = TRUE,
  col_options = NULL,
  col_stretch = FALSE,
  col_factor = FALSE,
  col_names = TRUE,
  col_readonly = NULL,
  col_hide = NULL,
  row_bind = NULL,
  row_edit = TRUE,
  save_as = NULL,
  title = NULL,
  logo = NULL,
  logo_size = 30,
  logo_side = "left",
  viewer = "dialog",
  viewer_height = 800,
  viewer_width = 1200,
  theme = NULL,
  read_fun = "read.csv",
  read_args = NULL,
  write_fun = "write.csv",
  write_args = NULL,
  quiet = FALSE,
  hide = FALSE,
  code = FALSE,
  cancel,
  track = NULL,
  log = NULL,
  autosave = TRUE,
  col_actions = TRUE,
  rules = NULL,
  ...
)

Arguments

x

a matrix, data.frame, data.table or the name of a csv file to edit. Tibbles are also supported. An empty table can be created by specifying the dimensions in a vector of the form c(nrow, ncol) or the names of the columns to include in the template. Database tables can be edited by supplying a dbplyr lazy table or a db_table().

col_bind

additional columns to add to the data prior to loading into editor, can be either an array containing the new data, a vector containing the new column names for empty columns or a named list containing a vector for each new column.

col_edit

logical indicating whether columns can be added or removed, set to TRUE by default.

col_options

a list named with valid column names and the input to use for each column:

  • c(TRUE, FALSE): checkboxes;

  • a vector of values, e.g. c("A", "B", "C"): a dropdown menu;

  • "date" or "datetime": a date or date-time picker (the column is returned as Date or POSIXct);

  • "time": a time picker ("HH:MM" text);

  • "textarea": text over several lines;

  • "password": hidden text;

  • "url": web addresses with a button to open them;

  • "colour" (or "color"): colours shown with a swatch;

  • c(min = 0, max = 10, step = 1) (any of the three): numbers within limits;

  • "slider": a slider and bar for numbers from 0 to 100;

  • "rating": a rating from 0 to 5 stars.

Set the limits of a slider with c(type = "slider", min = 0, max = 1, step = 0.05) and the number of stars of a rating with c(type = "rating", stars = 10) (a list() works too). Values outside the limits are marked in the editor and cannot be entered.

col_stretch

logical indicating whether columns should be stretched to fill the full width of the display, set to FALSE by default.

col_factor

logical indicating whether character columns should be converted to factors prior to returning the edited data, set to FALSE by default. Factor columns in the data are always returned as factors with their levels; new values become new levels after the existing ones.

col_names

logical indicating whether column names can be edited or a vector of column names that cannot be edited, set to TRUE by default to allow editing of column names.

col_readonly

names of columns that cannot be edited. Values and names of these columns are locked in the grid.

col_hide

names of columns to hide from the editor. Hidden columns will not be visible or editable but will be retained in the returned data.

row_bind

additional rows to add to the data prior to loading into editor, can be either an array containing the new data, a vector containing the new row names for empty rows or a named list containing a vector for each new column.

row_edit

logical indicating whether rows can be added or removed, set to TRUE by default.

save_as

name of a csv file to which the edited data should be saved.

title

optional title to show in the header, set to the name of the data by default.

logo

optional logo to include next to the title, supplied as the path or URL of an image. No logo is shown by default.

logo_size

width of the logo in pixels, set to 30 pixels by default.

logo_side

can be either "left" or "right" to determine the position of the logo relative to the title, set to "left" by default.

viewer

can be either "dialog", "browser" or "pane" to open the application in a dialog box, browser or RStudio viewer pane. First letter abbreviations are allowed, set to "dialog" by default. A function accepting the application URL can also be supplied.

viewer_height

numeric to control the height of the viewer in pixels when viewer is set to "dialog", set 800 by default.

viewer_width

numeric to control the width of the viewer in pixels when viewer is set to "dialog", set to 1200 by default.

theme

a Bootstrap 5 Bootswatch theme name (e.g. "yeti") or a bslib::bs_theme() object. Set to NULL by default to use the DataEditR theme.

read_fun

name of the function to use to read in the data when x is the name of a file, set to read.csv by default.

read_args

a named list of additional arguments to pass to read_fun.

write_fun

name of the function to use to write the edited version of x to a file, set to write.csv by default. Only requirement is that the first argument accepts the edited data and the second argument accepts the file name supplied to save_as.

write_args

a named list of additional arguments to pass to write_fun.

quiet

logical indicating whether messages should be suppressed, set to FALSE by default.

hide

logical indicating whether the Open and Export menus and the Done options should be hidden. When save_as is specified the edited data is written to file when Done is pressed.

code

logical indicating whether tidyverse code required to replicate the data edits should be printed to the console, set to FALSE by default. Alternatively, users can supply the name of an R script to write the code to. For data frames the generated code uses dplyr verbs such as rename(), select(), mutate(), slice(), and tibble::add_row(); for database tables it uses rows_update(), rows_append() and rows_delete().

cancel

optional value to return when the user hits the cancel button, set to the supplied data by default.

track

can be set to TRUE to highlight cells that have been edited or added to the original data with a default blue border, or a valid CSS color (e.g. "#FF0000" or "red") to use a custom border color. Set to NULL by default to disable highlighting.

log

name of a csv file to which the change log (who changed what and when, see dataEditLog()) is added when Done is pressed, with a first column data naming the data that was edited. The file is created if it does not exist, so the same file can keep the history of many editing sessions. A function can be supplied instead; it is called with the log as a data frame (for example to write it to a database). Set to NULL by default to not keep the log.

autosave

logical indicating whether changes should be saved as a draft while editing, set to TRUE by default. If the editor is closed without pressing Done or Cancel (the window was closed, R crashed, ...), opening the same data again offers to restore the changes. See the Drafts section.

col_actions

logical indicating whether the column menu offers actions that change a whole column: formulas (e.g. a new column kpl = mpg * 0.425), find and replace, recoding values, changing the type and sorting the rows. Each action is shown in the generated code as one dplyr verb. Set to TRUE by default.

rules

a list of rules the data should follow, each a one-sided formula that is TRUE for valid rows and named with the message to show, e.g. list("Age is between 0 and 120" = ~ age >= 0 & age <= 120, "End is after the start" = ~ end >= start). Cells that break a rule are marked in the grid and listed in the Problems tab, and Done asks before returning data with problems. Rules can also be added from a column's menu (Rules...). See the Validation section.

...

not in use.

Value

the edited data as a matrix or data.frame. For database tables the edited rows are returned as a data.frame after the changes have been committed.

Editing

Double-click a cell to edit it. Click and drag to select a range of cells, then copy (Ctrl+C), paste (Ctrl+V), clear (Delete) or fill down (Ctrl+D). Right click a row to insert or delete rows, and right click a column header to insert, rename, hide or delete columns. Double-click a column header to rename it. Ctrl+Z and Ctrl+Y undo and redo changes; press ? for the full list of shortcuts.

Layout

The toolbar opens other data (Open), shows or hides columns, lists active filters, searches the data (Ctrl+F), and opens the review panel, which lists every change with a button to revert it and shows the code that reproduces the edits. Type in the boxes under the column headers to filter rows. The status bar shows how many rows and columns are on screen and summarises the selected cells. The menu next to Done chooses whether all data or only what is on screen is returned.

Databases

Supply a dbplyr lazy table (e.g. dplyr::tbl(con, "artists")) or a db_table() to edit a database table. Rows are matched by primary key, changes are staged until you press Done, and you are asked to confirm before anything is written. Writes happen in a single transaction and are rolled back if any row was changed by someone else in the meantime. Adding, removing and renaming columns is disabled for database tables.

Change log and notes

Every change is recorded with the time and the user name. The History tab of the review panel lists the changes step by step and each step can be given a note, for example to say why a value was corrected. Supply log to keep this record in a file.

Drafts

With autosave = TRUE the changes are saved as a draft a moment after each edit. Drafts are kept in tools::R_user_dir("DataEditR", "data"); set options(DataEditR.drafts = ) to use another folder. A draft is removed when Done or Cancel is pressed, when it is restored or discarded, and after 30 days. Pressing Cancel asks for confirmation before changes are discarded.

Validation

Rules are checked after every change. Missing values pass a rule unless the rule says otherwise, so ~ end >= start only checks rows where both are filled in; add "Start is required" = ~ !is.na(start) to require a value. In the editor, a column's menu (Rules...) makes it required or unique, sets limits or a pattern, or adds a formula.

Column actions

A column's menu (or right-clicking its header) has actions that change the whole column: Formula... (a new column or new values from an R expression, e.g. round(mpg * 0.425, 1)), Find and replace..., Recode values..., Change type and sorting. Each shows a preview and is recorded as one dplyr verb, so the generated code reads mutate(kpl = round(mpg * 0.425, 1), .after = mpg) rather than listing every value. Formulas can use column names and common functions (arithmetic, round(), ifelse(), paste(), case_when(), as.Date(), ...), but not other code.

RStudio add-in

data_edit() is also available from the RStudio Addins menu as Interactive Data Editor. Highlight the name of a data frame, matrix or database table in the source editor or console and run the add-in to open it in the editor; with nothing highlighted an empty table is opened. The add-in can be bound to a keyboard shortcut through Tools > Modify Keyboard Shortcuts.

if(interactive()) {

  data_edit(mtcars)

}
